hypotheses.statement: Management view: moving 100% of packaging to Supplier B saves 3.0 EUR M a year
hypotheses.implication: The business case must be restated before any budget books the saving

hypotheses.statement: The proposal applies the 12% to the full 25 EUR M, including 1.1 EUR M of rush freight that no unit-price reduction touches
hypotheses.implication: The gross price lever is 2.868 EUR M a year, not 3.0

hypotheses.statement: Supplier B's single-plant risk erodes a material part of the saving once volume is concentrated
hypotheses.implication: Expected stoppage cost must be charged to every option in proportion to its Supplier B share

hypotheses.statement: A 70/30 split (Supplier B / incumbent) delivers more risk-adjusted value than 100% Supplier B
hypotheses.implication: 70/30 is a resilience premium of about 1.7 EUR M over three years, worth it only if stoppage cost runs at more than 2.4x history

hypotheses.statement: Keeping the status quo (30% Supplier B) is the safe, no-cost option
hypotheses.implication: The status quo forgoes all price saving and still carries 1.2 EUR M of expected stoppage cost

hypotheses.statement: The incumbent can absorb a Supplier B stoppage, so concentration risk is mitigable
hypotheses.implication: Cover needs two weeks' notice while past stoppages lasted 9-14 days, and under 100% Supplier B the relationship would lapse: a standby agreement is a gate, not a given
